web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Normal People by Sally Rooney
web_evidence.note: A sustained opening excerpt, reproduced with the copyright holder's permission, narrates Marianne and Connell as she and he while entering Connell's perceptions.

web_evidence.title: Glimpses of Utopia: Sally Rooney's Couples
web_evidence.note: The London Review of Books explicitly describes Normal People as third person, alternating close focalization between Marianne and Connell.

web_evidence.title: Conversations with Sally Rooney: the 27-year-old novelist defining a generation
web_evidence.note: The Guardian describes the novel's scenes across 2011–2015 and reproduces an interior passage that sustains he/she narration while entering Connell's mind.

web_evidence.title: Beautiful World, Where Are You?
web_evidence.note: The Sewanee Review explicitly states that Normal People is told in close third person and contrasts that intimate method with Rooney's later remote-third narration.

search_log: Searched: "Normal People Sally Rooney official excerpt publisher"; found and opened the permission-based BookBrowse opening excerpt and publisher catalog pages.
Searched: "Normal People Sally Rooney third person narration point of view"; found and opened explicit whole-book descriptions in the London Review of Books and Sewanee Review.

Searched: "Normal People Sally Rooney narrative perspective scholarly third person"; a Taylor & Francis article described an omniscient intimate voice and separate Marianne/Connell perspectives in search results, but the full article returned 403 and was not used as evidence.

Searched publisher-specific queries on Faber, Penguin, and Penguin Random House; their accessible title pages verified the work but did not provide usable sustained prose, so they were not included as person evidence.
Searched Guardian coverage and opened its Sally Rooney interview, which includes an interior third-person passage and describes the novel's multi-year scene structure.

Targeted searches for epistolary, diary, frame-narrative, multiple-narrator, and alternating-person structures produced no credible evidence that the novel contains sustained base narration in another grammatical person.
person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly presents sustained close narration of Marianne and Connell as she and he, with access to each character's private thoughts and perceptions. First-person forms occur in dialogue or gnomic material, while generic you appears in maxims, direct address, or analogies rather than as story-specific base narration. The authorized opening excerpt independently shows the same third-person mode, and credible whole-book criticism explicitly identifies alternating focalization between Marianne and Connell within third-person narration. Alternating focal characters therefore do not constitute alternating grammatical person. No credible source indicates a first-person frame, epistolary base, or sustained second-person section; the only limitation is that the Tier A prose source covers the opening, offset by extensive interior and ending quote evidence plus multiple explicit whole-book descriptions.
